system_description.narrative_title: Crisis, Capital and Code: Markets, Energy and Tech in Flux
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is being reshaped by simultaneous security shocks, energy reconfigurations and a rapid technology arms race. Regional conflicts (notably US–Iran and Russia–Ukraine) are driving oil and shipping disruptions that transmit into a bond-market panic and higher borrowing costs, while states and corporations race to lock in energy supplies and strategic footholds (eg. Venezuela). Parallel to this, an accelerating AI and data‑centre buildout concentrates technological capacity in a few states and firms, creating new economic leverage and supply‑chain dependencies. The system is therefore an interdependent cascade: geopolitical violence, commodity flows, financial stress and tech consolidation feed back on one another, raising global volatility and policy trade‑offs.
system_description.scope: Nation states and alliances; regional security hotspots and military deployments; global commodity markets (oil, LNG, shipping lanes); international financial markets (sovereign debt, bond yields, central bank policy); major technology firms, data centres and AI supply chains; multinational corporations and strategic investments; international institutions and diplomatic channels.
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio‑economic‑political system (the global civilization system integrating economic, security, technological and environmental subsystems).
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy & commodity markets (oil, LNG, shipping lanes)
Global financial & monetary system (bond markets, central banks, sovereign borrowing)
Global technology & AI industrial ecosystem (data centres, hyperscalers, chip and cloud supply chains)

variables.name: US–Iran military escalation
variables.description: United States and Iran have moved from intermittent strikes to sustained tit‑for‑tat military exchanges, shifting regional deterrence dynamics and force posture.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in an attritional war with intensified drone, missile and cyber campaigns that are reshaping European defence burdens and alliance support.

variables.name: China's technology and trade push
variables.description: China is accelerating industrial policy, AI and overseas tech expansion, provoking coordinated pushback from trading partners and shifting rules for global technology supply chains.

variables.name: Global sovereign bond shock
variables.description: Global bond markets and central banks are undergoing a regime shift as rising yields—driven by inflation, commodities and policy repricing—raise sovereign borrowing costs and force monetary recalibrations.

variables.name: Energy geopolitics and supply reconfiguration
variables.description: Venezuela's reintegration into markets and OPEC+ output choices, combined with repeated tanker attacks and maritime chokepoint disruptions, are reconfiguring global oil flows and market volatility.
